mainEntity.name: How much does a Range Rover Velar P550 engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Range Rover Velar P550 engine replacement typically costs £5,500-£10,500 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, with fitted prices ranging from £7,000-£14,000 depending on the workshop. Used engines: £3,500-£5,500 (supply only). Reconditioned: £5,500-£8,000 (supply only). Rebuilt with warranty: £7,000-£10,500 (supply only).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a Range Rover Velar P550?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning is a rattling or slapping noise from the engine on cold start. Other symptoms include engine misfire or rough running, Engine Management Light illumination, and loss of power or restricted performance. If you hear chain rattle, have the car inspected immediately - continued driving can cause catastrophic engine damage.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Range Rover Velar P550?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - the Velar P550 retains strong value, with 2018-2020 examples typically worth £32,000-£45,000 and newer models from £38,000 upwards. A rebuilt engine at £7,000-£10,500 represents 15-25% of the vehicle's value, making replacement a sound financial decision compared to scrapping or selling as a non-runner.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Range Rover Velar P550 engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full Range Rover Velar P550 engine replacement typically takes 3-7 days. A used engine swap takes 1-2 days. A rebuilt/reconditioned engine supply and fit takes 5-10 days (including rebuild time) plus 2 days for fitting.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the Range Rover Velar P550 and P400?

acceptedAnswer.text: The P400 uses a 3.0-litre six-cylinder mild-hybrid petrol engine producing 400hp, while the P550 uses the 5.0-litre supercharged V8 producing 550hp. The P550 is substantially quicker (0-60mph in 4.3 seconds vs 5.5 seconds), but also significantly thirstier (23mpg vs 27-28mpg). The engine codes are completely different - AJ133 for the P550 versus the six-cylinder Ingenium unit in the P400.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt Range Rover Velar P550 engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Rebuilt engines also include upgraded components addressing the original failure points (such as revised timing chain tensioners and supercharger isolators). Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier.

historyTimeline.h2: Range Rover Velar P550 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Range Rover Velar P550 launched in 2018 as the flagship performance variant of the Velar range, sitting above the P400 and P250 petrol models. It brought the 5.0-litre supercharged V8 from the larger Range Rover Sport SVR into the Velar's more svelte, design-led package - a genuine wolf in sheep's clothing.

commonProblems.h2: Range Rover Velar P550 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Range Rover Velar P550 uses the 508PS AJ133 5.0-litre supercharged V8 - a performance-oriented engine that shares its fundamental design with the larger Range Rover Sport SVR. While powerful and characterful, it has several well-documented failure points that Velar P550 owners should be aware of. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Why the Range Rover Velar P550 AJ133 Wears Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner design on the AJ133 V8 can fail, allowing the chain to stretch or jump timing. This is often exacerbated by extended oil service intervals - the tensioner relies on clean oil pressure to function correctly.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of timing chain, tensioners, and guides
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before engine damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain failure has caused valve/piston damage or engine has seized

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Range Rover Velar P550 retains strong value - 2018-2020 examples typically sit in the £32,000-£45,000 bracket, with newer 2024-2025 models from £38,000 upwards. Reconditioned engine replacement cost represents approximately 15-25% of vehicle value, making replacement financially viable in most cases. Given the premium nature of the P550, a full rebuilt engine with warranty is usually the recommended route.
problems.recommendation: If you catch timing chain rattle early, a chain replacement kit (tensioners, guides, chain) is the sensible first step - it's substantially cheaper than a full engine replacement. However, if the engine has already jumped timing or seized, a rebuilt unit with upgraded components is the only safe option. The Velar P550's high retained value means replacement is almost always justified over scrapping.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 508PS AJ133 Range Rover Velar P550 engine prices

problems.h4: Supercharger Isolator Wear - A Common Rattle Source in the Range Rover Velar P550
problems.rootCause: The supercharger drive isolator (torsional isolator) can wear, causing a 'clattering' or 'knocking' noise from the engine bay. This is caused by wear to the isolator spring support shaft, creating excessive backlash in the supercharger drive.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of the torsional isolator and related components
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early, before supercharger damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete supercharger overhaul with new bearings, seals, and isolator
repairOptions.longevity: When isolator failure has caused secondary damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Same as above - the Velar P550's strong retained value means repair and replacement costs are well within the vehicle's worth.
problems.recommendation: The supercharger isolator is a known weak point but is relatively inexpensive to address if caught early. Listen for a rattle that changes with engine speed - if present, have a specialist inspect the supercharger drive immediately.
